'''''Ulex densus''''' ([[Portuguese language|Portuguese]]: '''''tojo-gatunho''''' or '''''tojo-da-charneca''''')<ref>{{cite web |title=Ulex densus |url=https://gd.eppo.int/taxon/ULEDE |publisher=[[EPPO Global Database]] |access-date=13 December 2020}}</ref> is an evergreen shrub in the family [[Fabaceae]] [[endemic]] to [[Portugal]].

==Description==
''Ulex densus'' is an evergreen shrub up to {{convert|0.5|m|ft|abbr=on}} in height. It is densely ramified and forms a compact, closed pillow with dry brown stems and a bright green outside. It has spines up to {{convert|3|cm|in|abbr=on}} long and secondary spines up to {{convert|1.5|cm|in|abbr=on}}. Fruits are as large as the plant's [[Calyx (botany)|calyx]] and have 1-2 seeds.<ref name=floraiberica>{{cite web |title=Ulex densus |url=http://www.floraiberica.es/floraiberica/texto/pdfs/07_18%20Ulex.pdf |publisher=[[Flora Iberica]] |access-date=13 December 2020}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Ulex densus'' grows in the central-west coast of Portugal, mainly on the [[Lisbon District]], southern [[Leiria District]] and in the [[Arrábida Natural Park]]. It lives in woods and cliffs along the coast, but also ''Quercus'' forests (''[[Quercus rotundifolia]]'' and ''[[Quercus suber]]'') more inland, from sea level to {{convert|250|m|ft|abbr=on}} altitude and prefers [[limestone]] substrates.<ref name="iucn status 20 November 2021" /><ref name=floraiberica /><ref name="flora-on">{{cite web |title=Ulex densus Welw. ex Webb |url=https://flora-on.pt/#/1Ulex+densus |publisher=Flora-on |access-date=13 December 2020}}</ref>

==Threats==
It is mainly threatened by [[quarries]], urbanisation, industrial or commercial areas, communication networks, trampling, overuse and natural fires.<ref name="iucn status 20 November 2021" />
